title: Egg form obeys p_n + T(1/r + 1/r′) = P, the equation of all eggs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Egg form obeys p_n + T(1/r + 1/r′) = P, the equation of all eggs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The shape of an egg, as an extensible membrane filled with incompressible fluid under external pressure, obeys p_n + T(1/r + 1/r′) = P (external normal pressure plus membrane tension times total curvature equals internal pressure), which Thompson calls the equation of all eggs.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: p_n + T/r + T'/r' = P; with equal tensions p_n + T(1/r + 1/r') = P

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In fact, in so far as the postulates correspond near enough to actualities, the above equation is the equation of _all eggs_ in the universe.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Equation of the egg”. Scope: all hard-shelled and membrane-bound eggs

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: p_n + T/r + T'/r' = P; with equal tensions p_n + T(1/r + 1/r') = P

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-06: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The equation is explicit and falsifiable, but shape alone leaves too many unknown fields to test it. Existing museum geometry cannot provide a noncircular estimate of all terms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For eggs sampled before shell hardening, jointly measure local principal curvatures, external normal pressure, membrane tension and internal pressure, then test pointwise closure of the equation and compare residuals with richer anisotropic-shell models. Systematic nonzero residuals beyond measurement error would refute the asserted law.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public datasets lack co-registered membrane tension and pressure fields.

Hard shells violate the extensible-membrane postulate.

Material anisotropy and spatially varying thickness are plausible omitted terms.

analysis feasibility: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.62

data adequacy: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Egg outlines sufficient to compute the two principal curvatures are available for most bird families. The equation also contains external pressure, membrane tension, and internal pressure, none of which are measured, and if tension and external pressure may vary freely the equation is the equilibrium condition of a membrane rather than a restrictive law. A test with predeclared constraints on those fields is feasible and only partly identifies the equation Thompson calls the equation of all eggs.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For measured egg profiles, solve p_n + T(1/r + 1/r′) = P under an explicit constraint on tension and external pressure, and compare residuals with purely geometric oval equations. The physical equation is supported only if a constrained pressure and tension field fits and the unconstrained alternative does not; with T and p_n both free, essentially any axisymmetric egg can be made to satisfy the equation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A free tension function can absorb almost any smooth profile, which makes an unconstrained fit uninformative.

Internal pressure and membrane tension during shell formation are not in any of the shape archives.
